scenario.name: Microsoft Threat Intel, Wiz & CISA — Storm-0558: Acquired MSA Consumer Signing Key & Forged OWA/Exchange Online Tokens
scenario.shortSubtitle: Microsoft Threat Intel · CISA AA23-193A · Wiz · Crash Dump MSA Key · Cross-Scope Token Validation Flaw
scenario.overview: Picture an international border crossing checkpoint with glass passport inspection booths, zig-zag queue stanchions, an X-ray luggage conveyor belt, and a striped crossing barrier. Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station, then leaves a telltale trail inside the customs passport registry. A secondary customs officer cross-checks the border passport registry and catches a stamp serial number that was never issued by that embassy. In this scenario (T1606.002, Microsoft Threat Intel, Wiz & CISA, Storm-0558: Acquired MSA Consumer Signing Key & Forged OWA/Exchange Online Tokens), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: extracting the 2016 MSA Consumer Signing Key, then bypassing Enterprise Realm Isolation, then exfiltrating Diplomatic Mailboxes via OWA. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Extracting the 2016 MSA Consumer Signing Key, then Bypassing Enterprise Realm Isolation, then Exfiltrating Diplomatic Mailboxes via OWA, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: OFFLINE TOKEN FORGERY USING CRASH-DUMP MSA SIGNING KEY
stages.subtitle: Signing enterprise user claims with an acquired 2016 Microsoft Account (MSA) consumer key
stages.description: Approaching the international border crossing, a traveler steps up to the glass passport booth carrying a travel booklet with a subtly altered entry stamp. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the border customs officer's station while everyday visitors and the border customs officer go about their routine. As detailed in Microsoft’s root-cause investigation, a 2021 consumer signing service crash accidentally included private key material for a 2016 Microsoft Account (MSA) consumer signing key inside a process crash dump (which failed to be redacted due to a race condition and was later exfiltrated from a compromised engineer’s corporate environment). Storm-0558 uses this RSA private key offline to cryptographically sign forged authentication tokens populated with target enterprise user claims. Because token forgery happens 100% offline using the stolen private signing key, the attacker never sends a password guess or MFA push to Microsoft Entra ID, generating zero failed-login alerts. In the documented HTTPS OWA_AUTH exchange from Storm-0558 Forgery Engine to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with RESP HTTP 200 OK (confirming that the FORGED_MSA_TOKEN_PRESENTED request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 CROSS-REALM VALIDATION BYPASS IN EXCHANGE ONLINE / OWA). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ FORGED_MSA_TOKEN_PRESENTED / ⇠#1 RESP HTTP 200 OK) from Node ① (#1 Storm-0558 Forgery Engine) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Purview Audit & CISA AA23-193A Hunter).

stages.title: CROSS-REALM VALIDATION BYPASS IN EXCHANGE ONLINE / OWA
stages.subtitle: OWA accepts consumer MSA key signature for enterprise Azure AD user identity
stages.description: While the customs scanner checks only the outer cover of the passport, the forged interior page clears the glass booth and the striped crossing barrier swings upward. Here in Step 2 inside the border control, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the passport glass inspection booth without disturbing the diplomatic sealed pouch lane. When Storm-0558 sends the forged token to Outlook Web Access (outlook.office365.com/owa/), the OWA token validation library verifies the RSA signature against a shared metadata store containing both consumer MSA keys and enterprise Azure AD (Entra ID) keys (failing to enforce scope/issuer-realm isolation that should reject a consumer MSA signing key when validating an enterprise organizational user). OWA then exchanges the forged token for live Exchange Online session tokens under AppId 00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000. As Wiz Research highlighted, cryptographic signature verification alone is insufficient in multi-tenant cloud architectures unless the verifier strictly binds each signing key ID (kid) to its authorized issuer realm. In the documented OWA TOKEN_EXCHANGE exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Exchange Online / OWA Validator, Exchange Online / OWA Validator responds with ALERT SESSION_ISSUED (confirming that the ENTERPRISE_SESSION_MINTED request succeeded on Exchange Online / OWA Validator and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 SILENT OWA MAILBOX COLLECTION & CISA AA23-193A DETECTION). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ ENTERPRISE_SESSION_MINTED / ⇠#2 ALERT SESSION_ISSUED) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Exchange Online / OWA Validator), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Purview Audit & CISA AA23-193A Hunter).

stages.title: SILENT OWA MAILBOX COLLECTION & CISA AA23-193A DETECTION
stages.subtitle: Exfiltrating email via OWA service.svc while Purview logs anomalous MailItemsAccessed AppIds
stages.description: Rolling luggage smoothly off the X-ray conveyor into the secure arrival hall, the traveler crosses the border wearing an official-looking entry clearance. In this final step inside the border control, the intruder leaves a telltale trail inside the customs passport registry until the customs passport registry catches the mismatch. Routing traffic through SoftEther VPN residential exit nodes (198.51.100.119), Storm-0558 invokes /owa/service.svc?action=FindItem and action=GetItem to download sensitive diplomatic and government emails. A Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agency detects the intrusion by hunting in Microsoft Purview’s MailItemsAccessed unified audit log (spotting ClientInfoString="Client=OWA;Action=ViaProxy" and AppId 00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000 from anomalous VPN IPs with zero matching interactive Entra ID sign-ins). In response to this federal agency discovery, Microsoft revoked the compromised MSA key, patched cross-realm token validation, and made Purview MailItemsAccessed logging available across standard M365 licensing tiers. In the documented PURVIEW MailItemsAccessed exchange from Exchange Online / OWA Validator to OWA Token-Minting API (/owa/), OWA Token-Minting API (/owa/) responds with RESP 342 Items Synced (confirming that the BULK_MAIL_EXFILTRATION request succeeded on OWA Token-Minting API (/owa/) and completing the final execution objective of Microsoft Threat Intel, Wiz & CISA, Storm-0558: Acquired MSA Consumer Signing Key & Forged OWA/Exchange Online Tokens). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ BULK_MAIL_EXFILTRATION / ⇠#3 RESP 342 Items Synced) from Node ③ (#3 Exchange Online / OWA Validator) to Node ④ (#4 OWA Token-Minting API (/owa/)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Purview Audit & CISA AA23-193A Hunter).

detectionRule.title: CISA AA23-193A Exchange Online OWA Token Minting Anomaly
detectionRule.ruleCode: CloudAppEvents | where ActionType == "MailItemsAccessed" | where RawEventData.AppId == "00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000" and isempty(RawEventData.ClientAppId)
